new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern in all variants of the Kaqchikel language is fixed, its function is demarcative, and its position is the final syllable (acute, i.e. last-syllable, stress). It is invariant under derivation. For that reason it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (ALMG); investigadores J. E. Ajsivinac Sián, Lolmay P. O. García Mátzar, M. Chacach Cutzal, I. E. Alonzo Guaján. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'äl. Chimaltenango: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala.
new_statements.locator: Fonología, sección 'Acento', p. 55 (exceptions pp. 56-57); footnote 48 gives the data source as 'Datos de la Variación Dialectal del Idioma Kaqchikel de la CLK'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. is the render of printed p.55 (header '55 FONOLOGIA'), section 'Acento'. The passage is there verbatim: 'El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva.' Footnote 48 reads in full 'Datos de la Variación Dialectal del Idioma Kaqchikel de la CLK, parte morfológica.' (the compiler dropped 'parte morfológica'; immaterial). p.56 confirms the exceptions as reported: penultimate stress in vakix, tukur, tata, nana, b'alam…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the last syllable of every word, in every Kaqchikel variety, including derived forms; it is demarcative, not contrastive. The OKMA grammar (García Matzar & Rodríguez Guaján 1997: 20, also held by the project) adds that enclitics (directionals) attached to verbs and statives take the stress. NOTE: this is a statement about Kaqchikel (kaqc1270) as a whole, not a description of the Cauqué mixed language itself; no opened source states stress for Santa María Cauqué specifically.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in ALMG 2004 or OKMA 1997 (Bennett 2018, held by the project under, reports no secondary stress for Kaqchikel).
new_statements.exceptions: ALMG 2004 p.56: penultimate stress 'no es muy común en la mayoría de variantes' but occurs in a few native words (vakix 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata 'sir', nana 'madam', b'alam 'jaguar', anxa 'garlic', janila 'very') and in Spanish loans that are paroxytone (anma 'soul', paxa, alb'ertix 'pea', xalma 'ladder'); p.56-57: an 'acento en sílaba pesada' pattern (stress on the first vowel followed by glottal closure in transitive verb forms) in very few words in the variants of Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas and Magdalena Milpas Altas (Santiago Sacatepéquez / Cauqué not among them).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (root, derived, compound words); invariant under derivation; OKMA 1997 notes enclitics attract stress, i.e. the domain extends over verb+enclitic groups. Bennett 2016 sec. 6.1 notes that some authors treat K'ichean final stress as phrase-level but argues it is present at word level.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Kaqchikel (kaqc1270) 'en todas las variantes', not the Cauqué mixed language as such. The Cauqué speech community (aldea Santa María Cauqué, municipio Santiago Sacatepéquez) is treated as a Kaqchikel dialect point in the OKMA dialect survey (Majzul et al. 2000, cited as 'Kaqchikel, Santa María Cauqué variety' in Bennett 2016 ex. (3)), and the ALMG 2004 grammar's CLK dialect data include Santiago Sacatepéquez (appendix text 'de la variante de Santiago Sacatepéquez (SANZ)'), but neither ALMG 2004 nor OKMA 1997 names Santa María Cauqué. The mixed language's grammatical base, K'iche' (kich1262), also has fixed final stress (Henderson 2012; Bennett 2016 sec. 6.1, files), so both parent languages agree; still, no opened source states stress for Cauqué itself. Stevenson 1990 (SIL) is the only Cauqué-specific description and was not obtainable.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469-514. doi:10.1111/lnc3.12148
sources.note: sec. 6.1 'Stress' (p.495): 'Final stress (36a) is the norm in K'ichean languages'; 'Kaqchikel.. follows the typical K'ichean pattern of final stress, but non-final stress occurs in both loanwords (anima) and in some native words (janila)'. Identity evidence: sec. 2.1 ex. (3) gives vowel contrasts of 'Kaqchikel, Santa María Cauqué variety' from Majzul et al. 2000, i.e. the Santa María Cauqué speech is treated as a Kaqchikel variety in the OKMA dialect survey. Nothing on Cauqué stress specifically.

sources.citation: García Matzar, Pedro (Lolmay) & José Obispo Rodríguez Guaján (Pakal B'alam). 1997 [1a reimpr. 2001]. Rukemik ri Kaqchikel chi': Gramática kaqchikel. Guatemala: Cholsamaj / OKMA. (archive.org/details/rukemik-ri-kaqchikel-chi-gramatica-kaqchikel-descriptiva-de-okma-cholsamaj)
sources.note: p.20: 'El Kaqchikel se caracteriza por tener acento fijo en una sílaba determinada. El acento es agudo, lo que significa que la acentuación siempre va a recaer en la sílaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta..)'; enclitics (directionals) on verbs/statives attract the stress; Spanish loans keep penultimate stress (kaxa, xara, anma); a few native exceptions (nana, tata; Comalapa janila; Iximche' b'ala). Kaqchikel-level (authors' own variants Tecpán and San Andrés Semetabaj); no mention of Santa María Cauqué.
